transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I'm here today because... I keep hearing these very clear voices. It happens in my apartment mostly, and sometimes if I'm in an empty museum room. It sounds exactly like women whispering from behind the walls, and they keep telling me which photographs belong in the archive. It's very real to me, so... that's why I needed to come in.
Do the voices ever talk about what you're thinking, or do they say that thoughts are being placed in your mind that aren't yours?
No, they don't do that. They just tell me about the photographs. They don't really say anything about my thoughts, or... or put thoughts in my head. It's just the whispering about the archive.
Do you believe the voices are real, or do you ever think they might be something that others wouldn't hear?

Well... I know they're real. I mean, I hear them as clearly as I hear you right now. But... I guess I've noticed that when other people are around, like if a friend comes over or someone else walks into the museum room, they don't seem to react. They don't hear them. So... I know they're real to me, but I'm starting to realize maybe no one else can hear them.
Besides the whispering voices, have you ever seen things or sensed anything else that others around you don’t seem to notice?

No, I haven't. It's just the voices. I've never seen anything that isn't there, or... or felt anything strange like that. It's really only the women whispering about the photographs. That's the only thing.
Do you have any beliefs or thoughts about why the voices are telling you about the photographs, or what might be causing them to speak to you?

Well... yes. I do know why. I'm convinced it has to do with the museum board and the city arts people. I know they've been monitoring my phone. They know that my Caribbean archive will completely change how the galleries tell the truth about the history here. 

I think the voices are tied to that, making sure I focus on the photographs. And... well, honestly, no one has shown me anything that proves otherwise. I know they are watching what I do with the collection.
Have you considered that your belief about the museum board and city arts people monitoring you might not be true, or do you feel certain it's happening despite what others say?

I am certain it's happening. I mean... I haven't really considered that it isn't true, because I am just completely convinced that the museum board and the city arts people have been monitoring my phone. 

They know exactly what I'm working on. They know my Caribbean archive will change how the galleries tell the truth about the history here. And... well, like I just said, no one has shown me a single piece of evidence that proves otherwise. People might not believe me, but until someone actually proves it isn't happening, I know they are watching me.
Do you ever feel that the museum board or city arts people are involved in other unusual or strange ways in your life, beyond monitoring your phone and the archive?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. It's... it's really just what I told you. They monitor my phone because of the archive, but they aren't involved in the rest of my life. I haven't seen them do anything else strange, no. Just the phone.
Have you ever had any other strong beliefs or suspicions about people or organizations that others might not agree with or find hard to believe?

Well, no, not really. I don't have suspicions about anyone else. It's... it's just what we've been talking about. I am just absolutely convinced the museum board and the city arts people have been monitoring my phone. They know my Caribbean archive is going to change how the galleries tell the truth around here. And like I said, no one has shown me anything that proves otherwise. But no, there aren't any other groups or organizations I'm worried about. Just them.

Have you ever felt that your belief about the museum board and city arts people monitoring your phone has changed at all, or do you feel it with the same certainty all the time, even when others tell you there's no evidence for it?

No, it hasn't changed at all. I... I feel it with the exact same certainty every single day. Like I've been saying, I am just completely convinced that the museum board and the city arts people have been monitoring my phone. They know my Caribbean archive is going to change how the galleries tell the truth. It doesn't matter if people tell me there's no evidence, because no one has actually shown me anything that proves otherwise. So, no, my mind hasn't wavered on this. I know what is happening.

Even though no one has shown you proof that the museum board and city arts people are monitoring your phone, do you ever wonder if your belief might not be true, or do you feel absolutely certain it is true, no matter what others say?

I don't wonder if it's true, because I know it is. I am absolutely certain. Like I've said, I am completely convinced the museum board and the city arts people have been monitoring my phone. They know my Caribbean archive is going to change how the galleries tell the truth around here. It doesn't matter what anyone else says. No one has shown me a single piece of proof that they aren't doing it. So yes, I am absolutely certain it's happening.

Even when you're in different situations, like when you're with friends or at a completely unrelated event, do you still feel the exact same certainty that the museum board and city arts people are monitoring your phone, or does it ever feel less real or intense in those moments?

No, it doesn't... it doesn't fade or feel less real, no matter where I am. Even if I'm out with friends or at some completely unrelated event, the certainty is exactly the same. 

Like I keep telling you, I am just fully convinced that the museum board and the city arts people are monitoring my phone. That doesn't just turn off because I'm busy doing something else. They know my Caribbean archive is going to change how the galleries tell the truth around here. And since no one has shown me a single thing that proves otherwise, there is no reason for it to feel any less real to me.
Have you ever tried to test or confirm your belief in any way, like checking your phone for monitoring software or contacting someone for help with that?

I haven't taken it to anyone to check for software, no. I... I don't really feel the need to test it. 

Like I keep saying, I am just entirely convinced that the museum board and the city arts people are monitoring my phone. They know my Caribbean archive is going to change how the galleries tell the truth. I don't need to hunt for hidden programs or hire someone to know it's happening, especially since no one has shown me a single thing that proves otherwise.
How long have you believed that the museum board and city arts people have been monitoring your phone?

Well, it's been about eight months now. That's how long the voices... and this absolute certainty that people are watching my archive and my phone... that's how long it's all been present. About eight months.
Even if someone were to show you clear evidence that the museum board and city arts people are not monitoring your phone, would you still believe they are?

Yes, I would still believe it. I mean, I am completely convinced that the museum board and the city arts people are monitoring my phone. They know my Caribbean archive is going to change how the galleries tell the truth. Even if someone tried to show me evidence, it wouldn't change my mind, because I know what's happening. And like I said, no one has shown me anything that proves otherwise anyway.
